<a id="why"></a>

## Why

The project lead asked for a review of how graphs are embedded and whether search behaves well, given that an embedding groups things by language and the graph is a concept space. The review found that the design is sound and that paraphrase search works, but that label fields were being embedded and that a search reply gives an agent too little to act on. The rulings below followed in the same conversation.

<a id="evidence"></a>

## Evidence

| id | finding | measure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| e-01 | Label fields hold a large share of the vectors and each was an embedder call. | On a private graph of 536 nodes, 666 of 2,283 vectors (29%) were for label-like fields; one field with 3 distinct values had 536 vectors. Only one custom field, with 10 vectors, was prose. |
| e-02 | Label vectors flood the meaning leg and skew neighbourhoods. | A search for one label value returned 8 rows with the identical score, all matched on that field. 92% of each node's top 10 neighbours by meaning shared its label (34% by chance), against 39% sharing its type. |
| e-03 | The calibrated floor cuts almost nothing inside one graph. | 55% of all node pairs scored above the search floor of 0.409; the median pair scored 0.42. |
| e-04 | A search hit gives an agent nothing to judge by but the title. | A hit holds id, type, title, status and scoring fields; no node text, no links; the reply has no hints. |
| e-05 | Function words earn credit in the word leg. | For a question of 8 words, the two best matches by meaning (0.65 and 0.61) ranked 5th and 6th behind nodes matching 'what' and 'starts'. |
| e-06 | A short text does not score as itself. | A one-word query scored 0.71 against a field holding the same word. The cause is inferred, not confirmed. |
| e-07 | Meaning finds real links the graph does not have. | Only 13% of top 10 neighbours were already linked; the closest unlinked pairs were a technique and the artifact it produces (0.83 to 0.89). |

<a id="rulings"></a>

## Rulings

| id | ruling | by | date | why | not_chosen | change_if |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| r-01 | A custom string field is data by default and is embedded only when declared content. | project lead | 2026-11-16 | Label fields should not be included in vector search, and embedding them wastes calls to the embedder. A prose field wrongly left as data fails softly (words still find it); a label wrongly embedded fails loudly. | Keeping content as the default with a warning; switching a field's role automatically from its values. | Graph builders routinely forget to declare prose fields and the hint (search-05) does not catch it. |
| r-02 | No reranker and no other second model inside umx. | project lead | 2026-11-16 | The calling agent is already a capable model and is the judge. The tooling should be optimised so agents need fewer turns. | A small local reranker through the existing local model adapter (recommended by the reviewer, then withdrawn); a hosted rerank service. | Search gains a caller that is not a model and cannot judge hits itself. |
| r-03 | A search reply carries the matching text and the nearest links of each hit by default, and takes several phrasings in one call, labels strength in plain words, shows what the hits have in common, and gives hints throughout. | project lead | 2026-11-16 | An agent that does not know a flag exists gains nothing from it, so the useful form is the default. | Putting the text and links behind a flag. | The larger reply measurably costs agents more than the follow-up reads it saves (search-22). |
| r-04 | The std person fields job_title and org are data. | project lead | 2026-11-16 | They are short labels. | — | — |
| r-05 | Every such change updates the docs and the prompting in the skill in the same piece of work. | project lead | 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-16 | — | — | — |
